title: THE KING WAS HIDING.
paragraphs: THE KING WAS HIDING.

Not in battle.
Not in prayer.
Among the baggage.
(Yes. That’s in your Bible.)
In 1 Samuel 10, when Israel finally gets the king they begged God for, when destiny calls his name in front of the nation, when the prophet announces heaven’s choice…
They can’t find him.
So they ask the LORD.

And God says:
“He has hidden himself among the baggage.” (1 Samuel 10:22)
Let that sink in.

The anointed king.
Chosen by God.
Privately affirmed by the prophet.
Hiding behind luggage.
Why?
Because sometimes the loudest voice in the room isn’t the crowd.
It’s your insecurity.
Saul looked like a king. The Bible says he was handsome, taller than everyone else from the shoulders up (1 Samuel 9:2).

But height doesn’t silence fear.
Anointing doesn’t erase self-doubt.
Calling doesn’t cancel insecurity.

Some scholars interpret Saul’s hiding as humility.
But the pattern that unfolds later in his life suggests something deeper—fear of man, fragile identity, a heart not fully anchored in God.

He was crowned publicly…
but unsure privately.
And maybe that’s you.

You’re qualified.
Gifted.
Affirmed by others.

Yet when it’s time to step forward—
you hide.

Behind busyness.
Behind excuses.
Behind “I’m not ready.”
Behind spiritual language that sounds humble but smells like fear.
Imposter syndrome.
Feeling like you slipped past security into a calling you don’t deserve.
Let me speak to you as your brother.
The tragedy of Saul is not that he felt afraid.
The tragedy is that he never let God heal the fear.

He was anointed with oil in chapter 10…
but never fully surrendered his identity.
And when your identity is shaky, your leadership will be too.

Here’s the tension:
God chose Saul.
But Saul kept choosing insecurity.

And insecurity, when left uncrucified, becomes disobedience.
Disobedience becomes rebellion.
Rebellion becomes ruin.
That’s the slow burn of 1 Samuel.
But here’s where grace explodes into the story.
Because where Saul failed…
Jesus did not.
When heaven announced another King, He did not hide among baggage.

He stepped out of heaven into flesh.
He faced rejection, betrayal, humiliation.
He did not shrink back.
In the garden of Gethsemane, He felt the weight. Real anguish. Real pressure.
But instead of hiding, He prayed:
“Not My will, but Yours be done.” (Luke 22:42)
That’s the difference.

Saul hid from his calling.
Jesus embraced His cross.

And because He did—
you don’t have to hide anymore.
Listen carefully:

Your calling is not based on your confidence.
It’s based on Christ’s finished work.
You are not an imposter in God’s will if He is the One who called you.
But you must crucify the lie that says, “I’m not enough.”
Of course you’re not.
That’s why Jesus is.
The Gospel is not “Believe in yourself.”

The Gospel is:
Repent of self-reliance.
Trust in Christ alone.
Receive a new identity—sealed, secure, son or daughter of the King.
When your identity is anchored in Jesus, you can step out from behind the baggage.
Not because you feel ready.
But because He is faithful.
So today, hear the call.

Stop hiding.
Stop shrinking.
Stop apologizing for the grace on your life.

Bring your insecurity to the cross.
Lay it down.
And step forward in obedience.
Not as an imposter.
But as someone chosen, redeemed, and empowered by Christ.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
